BiblicalUsage: Gala means to be obstinate, to meddle where a man has no business. The beginning of strife is as when one lets out water, says Proverbs 17:14, so leave off contention before it is meddled with. A man who separates himself seeks and intermeddles with all wisdom in Proverbs 18:1, and it is an honour for a man to cease from strife, but every fool will be meddling, in Proverbs 20:3.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe meddling is the fool's work and ceasing from strife is the honourable work. The wise man leaves off contention before it floods, and I hold that the quarrels we refuse to start are the victories we never have to win.
